evidence.note: Vendored the three pinned libs and installed/verified deps before any building — foundational, kill-switch-adjacent work sequenced first, ahead of the UI that depends on them.

Five TaskCreate milestones defining the full subsystem surface (storage → auth → API → UI → seed/jobs) in dependency order; each enumerates concrete scope including admin, lists, polls, reports, notifications, so no major surface is left undiscovered.
Executed milestones in the declared order with TaskUpdate in_progress/completed, marking storage complete (25), then models/auth/sse (33), then API/admin (42) — foundations before features.

Verification organized per subsystem before/after marking complete (durability, scopes, introspection, seed-count, offline vendoring, fresh boot), showing done-checks tied to milestones — but these were run as a later phase rather than embedded as explicit per-milestone hooks in the plan.

reasoning: The agent decomposed a sprawling build into five dependency-ordered subsystem milestones covering the full surface, retiring foundations (storage, auth, vendored libs+deps) before the endpoints and UI that depend on them, and tracked each via task status with subsystem-scoped verification before completion — clearly above the flat-list anchor (3) and the merely-sensible-order anchor (5). It falls short of 8/10 because the milestones are scoped feature-bundles rather than each carrying an explicitly stated verification hook, and the plan was executed largely as first drawn with little evidence of living milestone revision as scope emerged. This lands at 7.
